| **AST & Spatial Maps** | `m_ast`, `m_ast_container`, `m_ast_include`, `m_bridge_tag`, `m_map_ast`, `m_tag` | Relational AST nodes, preprocessor `#include` links, container hierarchies, and coordinate regions (`line_s`, `char_s`, `line_e`, `char_e`); `m_map_ast.map_id` is the tag id, so the file token maps join `m_map_ast.map_id = m_bridge_tag.tag_id` |
| **Symbols & XRefs** | `m_symbol_def`, `m_symbol_ref` (views over `m_tag_def`, `m_tag_ref`, `m_blob_symbol`, `m_symbol_own`, `m_blob_symbol_def`, `m_blob_symbol_ref`; see `core/API.md`) | Definitions and usage cross-references (calls, field access, type usages, macro expansions). `def_id` of a definition stored once per tag is computed (not indexable) and `ref_id` may be NULL, so services select every needed column in the query that finds the rows instead of re-fetching by id. Rows of given target AST ids come from the engine's `symbol_refs_of_targets()` / `symbol_def_blobs_of_targets()` instead of `WHERE ast_id IN (...)` on the views, which takes seconds per target |
| **Kconfig** | `m_ast` (types `Kconfig_*`), `m_tag`, `m_bridge_tag` | Kconfig entries as tags (where each definition is, per blob and version). Menus, dependencies and values come from the semantic model built from Git per revision and ARCH (§4.4); there are no Kconfig tables |
| **Maintainers** | `m_maintainer_section`, `m_maintainer_member`, `m_maintainer_person`, `m_maintainer_pattern`, `m_maintainer_file`, `m_credits_entry` | Subsystem sections, pattern rules, maintainers, reviewers, and historical `CREDITS` biographies |
| **Git & Commits** | `m_commit`, `m_commit_file`, `m_bridge_commit_person`, `m_commit_parent`, `m_git_network`, `m_repository` | Commit metadata, DAG topology, modified files, multi-contributor trailers (Signed-off-by, Acked-by, Reviewed-by) |
| **System & State** | `m_db_instance` | Unique database instance hash (`instance_hash`, `created_at`) used by clients to detect database rebuilds |

## 6. Using the Services from Python

`webapp/main.py` is only the server's entrypoint (it exports `app`). Scripts and tests use the service classes
directly, one module per area under `webapp/backend/services/` (`FilesystemService`, `SymbolService`,
`KconfigService`, `MaintainerService`, `GitService`, `PaholeService`, `CallgraphService`, `DiffService`,
`history_service`, `mailing_list_service`), or the router functions under `webapp/backend/routers/`, whose
parameters carry plain defaults (`Annotated[..., Query()]`) so they can be called without FastAPI:

```python
from webapp.backend.services.symbol_service import SymbolService
from webapp.backend.services.kconfig_service import KconfigService

detail = SymbolService().get_symbol_detail("v3.0", "copy_process")
model = KconfigService().get_tree("v3.0", "x86_64")
```

---

## 7. Configuration & Execution

### 7.1. Configuration Precedence & Resolution
All database parameters, webapp server bindings, and parser options are resolved through
[`core.config`](core/config.py) following strict precedence:
$$\text{CLI Flags} > \text{Environment Variables} > \text{config.json} > \text{Built-in Defaults}$$

Environment variables synchronized via `core.config.sync_environ()` include:
- `DB_HOST` / `MYSQL_HOST` (default `"127.0.0.1"`)
- `DB_PORT` / `MYSQL_TCP_PORT` (default `3306`)
- `DB_USER` / `MYSQL_USER` (no default; a missing user is a configuration error when the connection is made)
- `DB_PASSWORD` / `MYSQL_PASSWORD` (no default; same)
- `DB_NAME` / `MYSQL_DATABASE` (default `"main"`)
- `WEBAPP_HOST` (default `"0.0.0.0"`)
- `WEBAPP_PORT` (default `8000`)
- `WEBAPP_RELOAD` (default `true`)
- `KERNELINFO_CACHE_DIR` (default `~/.cache/kernelinfo`; else config `cache.dir`): the disk cache of derived data and
  the cache engine's storage (§2.14); config `cache.engine` (default `"ram"`, also `"sqlite"`, env
  `KERNELINFO_CACHE_ENGINE`) selects the cache engine (`cache_engine/CACHE_API.md`)

Webapp keys of `config.json` beyond the bindings (`"webapp"` section):
- `cache.max_mb` (default `1024`): global cap of the disk cache (§2.14).
- `jobs.workers` (default `2`): background job worker threads per process (§2.15).
- `prewarm_indexes` (default `false`): build the commit relation and Kbuild object indexes at startup (§2.12).
- `tools.checkpatch.enabled` (default `false`), `tools.checkpatch.ref` (default `"latest-release"`, or a
  release tag) and `tools.sandbox` (default `""`, e.g. `"bwrap"`): running `scripts/checkpatch.pl` (§2.18).
- `source_index.workers` (default `2`): low-priority processes extracting the blobs the database's
  `m_blob_facts` lacks (call facts, §2.19, and Kernel API records, §4.9); `source_index.max_mb` (default
  `1024`): cap of each of their SQLite stores; `source_index.revisions` (default `8`): assembled revisions
  kept on disk (§2.19).
- `cve.repo_dir` (top-level `"cve"` section, default `"cvelistV5"`; a relative path is under the project
  root): local clone of the CVE list (`cvelistV5`) or of the kernel CNA's `vulns.git`, which the parser
  ingests for the CVE features (§4.11); the operator keeps it current. No clone there: the features are off.

The Git repository served by the webapp (`webapp/backend/config.py:LINUX_REPO_DIR`) is the default entry of
the `"repositories"` config list (`core.config.get_default_repo_path()`), auto-detected under
`workspace.repos_dir` (default `repos/`).

### 7.2. Starting the Server
Start the application from the repository root:

```bash
# Using webapp entrypoint (with CLI overrides; -c selects another config.json)
python3 webapp/main.py -c config.json --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --no-reload

# Or via uvicorn directly (CONFIG_FILE selects another config.json)
uvicorn webapp.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload
```

`-c` is passed on as the `CONFIG_FILE` environment variable before anything reads the configuration, so it
also applies to the process uvicorn's reloader starts. Options left unset fall back to the `webapp` section of
the configuration (`host`, `port`, `reload`).

Open `http://localhost:8000` in any modern browser.

## 8. Error Handling, Status Codes & Resilience

| HTTP Status Code | Scenario | Response Payload Format |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `200 OK` | Successful execution | `{ ... }` or `[ ... ]` JSON response |
| `202 Accepted` | A background job (§2.15) is still computing the answer; poll again after `retry_after_ms` (`Cache-Control: no-store`) | `{"state": "building", "key": "...", "progress": {"done": 3, "total": 10, "note": "..."}, "retry_after_ms": 1000}` |
| `400 Bad Request` | Directory traversal attempt (`..`), invalid parameter syntax, missing required fields | `{"detail": "Path traversal not permitted"}` |
| `403 Forbidden` | Access to files outside the repository jail (`LINUX_REPO_DIR`) | `{"detail": "Access to path outside repository jail is forbidden"}` |
| `404 Not Found` | Unknown kernel version, non-existent file/symbol/subsystem/commit | `{"detail": "File 'foo.c' not found for version 'v3.0'"}` |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Sliding-window rate limit exceeded (>600 requests / 60 seconds per IP) | `{"detail": "Rate limit exceeded. Try again in X seconds."}` |
| `503 Service Unavailable` | Text search busy: two greps already run for this repository and a third waited 5 s (§2.1.3) | `{"detail": "search busy, retry"}` |
| `500 Internal Error` | Database connection pool exhaustion or unhandled server exception | `{"detail": "Internal database error"}` |

### 8.1. Client-Side Offline Storage & Fallbacks (`IndexedDB`)
The frontend client falls back to IndexedDB (`KernelInfoIDE_v2`, v6, `webapp/frontend/js/db.js`; stores and
pruning in §5.5) whenever network operations fail or the server is temporarily offline:
- **`files` Store**: Cached file contents, AST tokens, directory trees, blame records, catalogs.
- **`symbols` Store**: Cached symbol search results, definition records, XRef usage graphs.
- **`kconfigs` Store**: Architecture trees, defconfig mappings, dependency graphs.
- **`maintainers` Store**: Maintainer sections, developer profiles, CREDITS catalog.
- **`commits` Store**: Commit listings, commit details, structured diffs.
- **`tools` Store**: NodeMap, treemap, callgraph and pahole results.
- **`mail` Store**: Public-inbox email messages, parsed patch diffs, thread message rosters, search result
  sets. Functions as an active read-through cache preventing duplicate network/SSH requests for identical
  emails, as well as an offline store.
- **`meta`, `tabs_state`, `nodemap_projects` Stores**: sync tokens and settings, saved tab sessions and
  layouts, NodeMap diagrams (user state, never purged by a sync token).
- **`user` Store** (v6, S06): bookmarks, notes, tours and watches — never pruned or cleared with the cache;
  only **Clear User Data** and **Full Local Reset** delete it (§5.5).
- Responses of background-job endpoints are stored only once final: `202 Accepted` progress bodies never are
  (§2.15).
